analysis.title: Treasury QRA: Flexible guidance
key_insights: Treasury's financing estimates are $618bn for Q4 26 and $800bn for Q1 27, with target cash balances of $850bn and $1.0trn. Adjusted for the cash balance change, Q1 27 borrowing is $650bn, about 17% above the $560bn in Q1 26. Barclays reads this as underlying borrowing needs rising on the margin.

Barclays expects Treasury to keep auction sizes and nominal coupons unchanged at the November 4 refunding. It sees little reason to cut sizes when borrowing needs are elevated and the long end has outperformed on the curve.

Barclays expects Treasury to change its forward guidance to 'maintaining overall nominal coupon and FRN auction sizes for the coming quarters', replacing 'at least the next several quarters'. 'Coming quarters' keeps a near-term anchor without extending the no-change commitment. 'Overall' signals that stable aggregate coupon issuance need not mean unchanged sizes at every tenor.

T-bill issuance is expected to rise further. Q1 needs are roughly $540bn net before Fed purchases and $440bn net to private investors. With money fund inflows stagnating, Barclays expects bill supply pressure to persist into Q1.

Barclays believes the Treasury investor base has become more price sensitive. Money funds remain a key source of front-end demand and banks should support short- to intermediate-maturity USTs. Pension funds and other traditional long-end buyers are less likely to grow in line with financing needs, so any coupon size increase is expected only up to the 10y sector.

Treasury asked dealers how to make the buyback program more effective. The program has been broadened to more counterparties, and Barclays suggests publishing the composition of participants, similar to the post-auction bidder and investor classifications.
Barclays expects TIPS sizes to be unchanged, with the November 10y reopening at $19bn, the December 5y reopening at $24bn and the January 10y reopening at $21bn.

Barclays keeps a tactical 10s30s Treasury curve steepener ahead of the November 4 refunding. It expects unchanged long-end sizes and guidance that stops short of signaling long-end cuts, which it says would disappoint the market.

Roll estimates for the when-issued 3y, 10y and 30y: fair value at settlement of 0.2bp, 0.6bp and -0.5bp, and at announcement 1.0bp, 0.9bp and -0.3bp. Assumed coupons are 4.625%, 4.875% and 5.25%. A coupon shift of 0.125% moves the curve by less than 0.1bp.
SOMA add-ons at the refunding auctions are expected at $11.8bn (3y), $8.5bn (10y) and $5.1bn (30y), out of $47.8bn of maturing principal reinvested across mid- and end-November auctions.

Recent auctions were strong at the 10y and 30y. The September and October 10y auctions stopped 1.4bp and 1.9bp through, against a 0.6bp six-month average stop-through. October bid-to-cover was 2.77x and primary dealers took a record-low 3%. The September 30y stopped 2.7bp through with foreign participation of 42%, and the October 30y tailed 0.3bp with 25% foreign participation.
